item.title: Russia And US Discussed Nuclear Arms And Agreed Talks Need To Start Soon, Kremlin Says
item.description: By VLADIMIR ISACHENKOV and JAMEY KEATEN Associated Press MOSCOW (AP) — Russian and U.S. negotiators discussed the expiration of the last remaining nuclear arms pact between the two countries and agreed on the need to quickly launch new arms control talks, the Kremlin said Friday. item.title: Rural Texas Decline
item.description: Around one-thousand people are moving to Texas every day, seeking the American dream. Data shows they’re settling in the suburbs. State Demographer Lloyd Potter says this is leading to an issue where rural areas becomes so sparse that it cannot support retail or health clinics. item.title: Gov Talks Walkouts
item.description: Texas Governor Greg Abbott is warning public school leaders that, if kids walk out of class to protest, the districts will face funding cuts and legal liability. Hundreds of students across Texas have been protesting ICE raids over the last week. The Texas Education Agency is investigating several districts to see if teachers and counselors encouraged the walk-outs.

item.title: Camp Sued Again
item.description: Yet another lawsuit has been filed against the owners of Camp Mystic in the Texas Hill Country. It was flooded last July, killing 27-campers and counselors. One of the kids, Cile Steward, is still missing. Her family claims the camp’s owners ignored a history of flooding. Their child was in a cabin that was not evacuated. The camp said in a statement that the wall of water was “unexpected and unforeseeable.”

item.title: Oil Gas Law
item.description: A Texas law meant to support the state’s oil and gas industry has been ruled unconstitutional. It was passed back in 2021, and banned state investments in funds that oppose fossil fuels. There’s already an appeal. Comptroller Kelly Hancock says the state has a right to “prevent investment firms from using Texan’s own money to push political agendas that would undermine our economy.”

item.title: Migrant Defense Suit
item.description: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton is suing Bexar County, trying to stop the funneling of taxpayer dollars to groups that defend illegal immigrants in court. Commissioner Grant Moody saw this coming from a mile away. He says there is not a hard dollar amount on how much the county spent on the effort. But, he thinks it’s close to two-million dollars.

item.title: FEMA Will Resume Staff Reductions That Were Paused During Winter Storm, Managers Say
item.description: By GABRIELA AOUN ANGUEIRA Associated Press The Federal Emergency Management Agency will resume staff cuts that were briefly paused during January’s severe winter storm, according to two FEMA managers, stoking concern across the agency over its ability to address disasters with fewer workers.
